bull_bear.body:
- Over five decades of experience — entered its 51st year of operations in FY 2025-26
- Installed track record of over 31,000 circuit km of transmission lines, over 1,800 bays of substations and electrification of over 37,000 villages
- Capability across the entire T&D value chain, including high voltage lines up to 800 kV and substations up to 765 kV
- Blue-chip customer base spanning public and private sector utilities — Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL
- Captive transmission tower manufacturing at Nashik with combined annual capacity of 72,000 MT after the Plant–II commissioning
- Owned state-of-the-art R&D tower-testing centre at Ghoti that is also monetised through third-party testing orders
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sustainable procurement / raw material supply-chain disruption — the only material issue the Company itself classifies as a risk with negative financial implications — BRSR material-issues table states: 'The Company recognizes the need to prevent disruptions that could be brought by social, natural or legal issues and to ensure ongoing raw material availability' and that 'The disruption to the supply chain may cause discontinuity or availability of the raw material which may affect the business operations.' No mitigation approach is disclosed ('NA' in the mitigation column).
- Single-activity concentration — 100% of turnover comes from one business activity — BRSR reports transmission and distribution / 'Construction, erection and maintenance of power and transmission lines' as 100% of turnover, leaving no diversification cushion if T&D EPC ordering slows.
- Customer and counterparty concentration in a small set of utilities and developers — Major clients are listed as Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL; EPC receivable and order-flow exposure is therefore concentrated in a handful of buyers.
- Geographic concentration — narrow domestic footprint and negligible export base — The Company serves 5 states nationally and 2 countries internationally, and exports contribute just 0.02% of total turnover, despite the MD&A citing international transmission opportunities in Asia, Africa and the Middle East as a growth avenue.
- Dependence on government policy, reforms and utility capex cycles for order inflow — The MD&A attributes the sector's growth prospects to favourable government policies, regulatory reforms, Green Energy Corridors and utility investment programmes; a slowdown or reform reversal in these programmes would directly compress the addressable EPC opportunity.
- Execution and project-delivery risk across diverse geographies and challenging site conditions — Management notes projects are 'executed across diverse geographies and challenging site conditions'; the business model depends on commissioning complex EHV/HVDC lines and substations on time and at quality.
- Human capital retention / attrition — Permanent-employee turnover was 17.53% in FY 2025-26 (25.45% in FY 2024-25, 25.76% in FY 2023-24); the Company itself states it 'recognizes talent as the primary source of its competitive edge' and is 'aiming at being employer of choice', which it has not yet achieved.
- Unassured ESG disclosure and low workforce diversity — The Company has not undertaken reasonable assurance of the BRSR Core (assurance provider and type both blank); women are 4.22% of total employees, 0% of workers, 16.67% of the Board and 25.00% of KMP.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Incorporated in 1974, JSL is an EPC contracting company building power transmission and distribution networks across India and global markets. The Company has three lines of operations — transmission lines, substations and rural electrification — with experience in executing high voltage transmission lines up to 800 kV and substations up to 765 kV, and it also manufactures transmission towers at its Nashik plants and offers tower testing services at its R&D Centre at Ghoti. Its major clients are Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Focus on operational excellence, disciplined project execution, financial prudence, innovation and sustainable value creation in power transmission infrastructure
- Leverage enhanced manufacturing capacity, experienced project execution teams and technical expertise to participate in large-scale domestic and international transmission projects
- Use the expanded Nashik manufacturing capacity to cater to growing customer demand, improve operational efficiencies and support long-term growth in the power transmission infrastructure sector
- Monetise and improve utilisation of the state-of-the-art R&D tower-testing centre at Ghoti by securing third-party transmission tower testing orders
- Strengthen presence in the Indian power transmission sector by securing turnkey EPC contracts for 765 kV / 800 kV AC, HVDC lines and 765 kV substations
- Pursue emerging opportunities beyond India in Asia, Africa and the Middle East where transmission infrastructure, renewable integration and grid modernisation programmes are being funded
- The routed text discloses no dividend or payout policy. Stated intent is directional only: the Board says the Company 'remains focused on enhancing operational excellence, strengthening financial performance, improving capital efficiency, fostering innovation and maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance', and management describes a 'sustained focus on profitability', 'effective cost management initiatives' and 'disciplined financial controls'. On capital structure, the 51st AGM notice proposes as special business an increase in the Authorised Share Capital from Rs.2,56,30,00,000 to Rs.3,20,00,00,000 through creation of 31,85,00,000 additional equity shares of Rs.2 each ranking pari passu with existing shares, with a consequential amendment to Clause V of the Memorandum of Association — indicating headroom being created for future equity issuance. No buyback, debt-reduction target or credit-rating commitment is disclosed.
- All policies mapped to the nine NGRBC principles are Board-approved, translated into procedures and extended to value-chain partners
- Certified to the international standards ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001 (IMS Certification), operated through the JSL HSE framework for implementation of the HSE system across JSL
- Organisational objectives are defined in alignment with the QSHE Policy and cascaded into departmental objectives and targets set by process owners with defined timelines; performance against sustainability goals and targets is reviewed periodically with corrective actions
- Efficient energy management identified as a material opportunity, with the Company increasing indigenous solar power generation and resultant consumption
- Energy conservation initiative: installation of solar lights
- Go Green initiative: tree plantation drives
- Digital integration: launch of the IMS Portal via intranet
- Health & hygiene: provision of bio-toilets at project sites and yoga sessions for employee well-being
- Safety & quality campaigns: observance of National Safety Day/Week, Fire Safety Week, Road Safety Week and Quality Month across JSL under the theme 'One Team – One JSL'
- Diversity & inclusion treated as a material opportunity — diversity committees and a separate cell established to work on D&I initiatives, with steps taken on representation of female colleagues and an international workforce
- Grievance redressal mechanisms embedded in the BRSR-linked policies for all stakeholder groups; NIL complaints filed and NIL pending across communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- Reasonable assurance of the BRSR Core has NOT been undertaken; no assurance provider named
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company completed its principal capacity expansion: commercial manufacturing operations commenced at the second unit, Nashik Plant–II, in January 2026, adding an annual manufacturing capacity of 36,000 MT. With this commissioning, the combined annual manufacturing capacity of Nashik Plant–I and Nashik Plant–II increased to 72,000 MT. Management states the expansion is expected to strengthen the Company's ability to cater to growing customer demand, improve operational efficiencies and support its long-term growth strategy in the power transmission infrastructure sector, and it cites 'enhanced manufacturing capacity' as a reason it is well placed to participate in large-scale domestic and international transmission projects. Alongside manufacturing, the Company's state-of-the-art R&D Centre at Ghoti was better utilised during the year through multiple third-party orders for transmission tower testing services, which contributed incremental revenue and improved profitability. On the execution side, key transmission assets were completed and commissioned during the year, including the 400 kV Pirana–Pirana LILO line at Ahmedabad (240 CKM HTLS line, supporting the 4.5 GW Khavda renewable energy evacuation system) and the 400 kV Gadag-II transmission line in Karnataka (100 CKM twin HTLS line, facilitating evacuation from the 1,500 MW Koppal Solar Energy Zone). No new capex project, capital outlay or future commissioning timeline beyond the completed Nashik Plant–II is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural growth in the EPC / T&D sector driven by rising electricity demand, rapid renewable energy integration, grid modernization initiatives and sustained investment in power infrastructure; significant growth opportunities expected during FY 2026-27 and beyond
- Infrastructure-led growth and rising power demand from urbanization, industrial expansion and growing electrification driving demand for transmission networks and substations
- Renewable energy integration and energy transition — solar, wind, hybrid and green hydrogen investments accelerating the need for transmission corridors, evacuation systems and grid connectivity
- Grid modernization and digital transformation — investments in smart grids, digital substations, advanced monitoring, automation and predictive maintenance
- Policy support and sector reforms — government initiatives on transmission capacity, improved payment discipline and utility financial health creating a favourable environment
- Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission system expansion and modernization of aging transmission assets expected to generate significant EPC opportunities
- Emerging international demand across Asia, Africa and the Middle East from energy security, cross-border interconnections and sustainable infrastructure investments
- Technology-driven transformation — digital technologies, artificial intelligence, data analytics and intelligent asset management reshaping project execution and asset reliability
- Company-specific levers: established track record in complex transmission projects, strong engineering capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure and a growing order book
- Opening order book as on April 1, 2026 was Rs.2,274 Crores
- From implementation of the Resolution Plan in November 2021 up to March 31, 2026, the Company generated aggregate total income of Rs.1,974 Crores through execution of its order book
- Major FY 2025-26 wins: turnkey EPC contracts for 765 kV & 800 kV AC and HVDC transmission lines and 765 kV substations in India aggregating Rs. 639.08 Crores
- 800 kV HVDC Bhadla–III to Fatehpur Transmission Line Project valued at Rs. 288.38 Crores
- EHV 220 kV / 110 kV Transmission Line Modification Works for the Mumbai Coastal Road Project valued at Rs. 88.35 Crores
- Multiple orders from various customers for transmission tower testing services at the R&D Centre at Ghoti, improving utilisation of testing infrastructure and contributing incremental revenue

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jyoti Structures Limited is one of India's leading engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies in the power transmission and distribution sector, with expertise across the entire T&D value chain in India and international markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 1974, JSL is an EPC contracting company building power transmission and distribution networks across India and global markets. The Company has three lines of operations — transmission lines, substations and rural electrification — with experience in executing high voltage transmission lines up to 800 kV and substations up to 765 kV, and it also manufactures transmission towers at its Nashik plants and offers tower testing services at its R&D Centre at Ghoti. Its major clients are Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- JSL Corporate Services Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% held by the listed entity); does not participate in the Company's Business Responsibility initiatives
- Jyoti Energy Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% held by the listed entity)
- Jyoti International Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); holding entity for Jyoti Americas LLC and Jyoti Structures Canada Ltd
- Jyoti Structures Africa (Pty) Limited — subsidiary: 70% held by the listed entity; South Africa-based (ZAR reporting currency)
- Jyoti Structures FZE — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); UAE-based (AED reporting currency) and parent of Jyoti Structures Namibia (Pty) Ltd
- Jyoti Structures Namibia (Pty) Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary, 70%; subsidiary of Jyoti Structures FZE
- Jyoti Structures Nigeria Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary, 100%
- Jyoti Structures Kenya Ltd. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary, 100%
- Jyoti Americas LLC — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary, 100%; subsidiary of Jyoti International Inc.
- Jyoti Structures Canada Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary, 100%; subsidiary of Jyoti International Inc.
- Gulf Jyoti International LLC — JV: Joint venture, 30% held by the listed entity
- GJIL Tunisia SARL — JV: Joint venture, 49% held by the listed entity
- Abchlor Investments Pvt. Ltd — related party: Enterprise owned/managed by directors; Mr. Abhinav Rishi Angirish is a director of Abchlor Investments Private Limited
- Bajel Electricals Ltd. — related party: Enterprise owned/managed by directors (IND AS 24 disclosure)
- RebelCorp Pvt. Ltd — related party: Enterprise owned/managed by directors; Mrs. Monica Akhil Chaturvedi holds a directorship in Rebelcorp Private Limited

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Transmission and Distribution (100% of turnover):** Construction/erection and maintenance of power and transmission lines, EHV / HVDC transmission lines up to 800 kV, Substations up to 765 kV, Distribution lines and rural electrification, Transmission tower testing services (R&D Centre, Ghoti)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian power transmission and distribution sector (5 states served)
- International markets (2 countries served; exports 0.02% of total turnover)
- Renewable energy evacuation and green energy corridor projects
- Public and private sector power utilities and developers — Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent, PGCIL

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural growth in the EPC / T&D sector driven by rising electricity demand, rapid renewable energy integration, grid modernization initiatives and sustained investment in power infrastructure; significant growth opportunities expected during FY 2026-27 and beyond
- Infrastructure-led growth and rising power demand from urbanization, industrial expansion and growing electrification driving demand for transmission networks and substations
- Renewable energy integration and energy transition — solar, wind, hybrid and green hydrogen investments accelerating the need for transmission corridors, evacuation systems and grid connectivity
- Grid modernization and digital transformation — investments in smart grids, digital substations, advanced monitoring, automation and predictive maintenance
- Policy support and sector reforms — government initiatives on transmission capacity, improved payment discipline and utility financial health creating a favourable environment
- Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission system expansion and modernization of aging transmission assets expected to generate significant EPC opportunities
- Emerging international demand across Asia, Africa and the Middle East from energy security, cross-border interconnections and sustainable infrastructure investments
- Technology-driven transformation — digital technologies, artificial intelligence, data analytics and intelligent asset management reshaping project execution and asset reliability
- Company-specific levers: established track record in complex transmission projects, strong engineering capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure and a growing order book
- Opening order book as on April 1, 2026 was Rs.2,274 Crores
- From implementation of the Resolution Plan in November 2021 up to March 31, 2026, the Company generated aggregate total income of Rs.1,974 Crores through execution of its order book
- Major FY 2025-26 wins: turnkey EPC contracts for 765 kV & 800 kV AC and HVDC transmission lines and 765 kV substations in India aggregating Rs. 639.08 Crores
- 800 kV HVDC Bhadla–III to Fatehpur Transmission Line Project valued at Rs. 288.38 Crores
- EHV 220 kV / 110 kV Transmission Line Modification Works for the Mumbai Coastal Road Project valued at Rs. 88.35 Crores
- Multiple orders from various customers for transmission tower testing services at the R&D Centre at Ghoti, improving utilisation of testing infrastructure and contributing incremental revenue

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Focus on operational excellence, disciplined project execution, financial prudence, innovation and sustainable value creation in power transmission infrastructure
- Leverage enhanced manufacturing capacity, experienced project execution teams and technical expertise to participate in large-scale domestic and international transmission projects
- Use the expanded Nashik manufacturing capacity to cater to growing customer demand, improve operational efficiencies and support long-term growth in the power transmission infrastructure sector
- Monetise and improve utilisation of the state-of-the-art R&D tower-testing centre at Ghoti by securing third-party transmission tower testing orders
- Strengthen presence in the Indian power transmission sector by securing turnkey EPC contracts for 765 kV / 800 kV AC, HVDC lines and 765 kV substations
- Pursue emerging opportunities beyond India in Asia, Africa and the Middle East where transmission infrastructure, renewable integration and grid modernisation programmes are being funded
- The routed text discloses no dividend or payout policy. Stated intent is directional only: the Board says the Company 'remains focused on enhancing operational excellence, strengthening financial performance, improving capital efficiency, fostering innovation and maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance', and management describes a 'sustained focus on profitability', 'effective cost management initiatives' and 'disciplined financial controls'. On capital structure, the 51st AGM notice proposes as special business an increase in the Authorised Share Capital from Rs.2,56,30,00,000 to Rs.3,20,00,00,000 through creation of 31,85,00,000 additional equity shares of Rs.2 each ranking pari passu with existing shares, with a consequential amendment to Clause V of the Memorandum of Association — indicating headroom being created for future equity issuance. No buyback, debt-reduction target or credit-rating commitment is disclosed.
- All policies mapped to the nine NGRBC principles are Board-approved, translated into procedures and extended to value-chain partners
- Certified to the international standards ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001 (IMS Certification), operated through the JSL HSE framework for implementation of the HSE system across JSL
- Organisational objectives are defined in alignment with the QSHE Policy and cascaded into departmental objectives and targets set by process owners with defined timelines; performance against sustainability goals and targets is reviewed periodically with corrective actions
- Efficient energy management identified as a material opportunity, with the Company increasing indigenous solar power generation and resultant consumption
- Energy conservation initiative: installation of solar lights
- Go Green initiative: tree plantation drives
- Digital integration: launch of the IMS Portal via intranet
- Health & hygiene: provision of bio-toilets at project sites and yoga sessions for employee well-being
- Safety & quality campaigns: observance of National Safety Day/Week, Fire Safety Week, Road Safety Week and Quality Month across JSL under the theme 'One Team – One JSL'
- Diversity & inclusion treated as a material opportunity — diversity committees and a separate cell established to work on D&I initiatives, with steps taken on representation of female colleagues and an international workforce
- Grievance redressal mechanisms embedded in the BRSR-linked policies for all stakeholder groups; NIL complaints filed and NIL pending across communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- Reasonable assurance of the BRSR Core has NOT been undertaken; no assurance provider named
